transcript.text: In this tutorial, we'll walk you through how to enable and manage multiple languages across your on Print Shop storefront.
This includes everything from static content and product details to design templates, CMS pages, and SEO data.
Let's start with enabling multiple languages.
If you'd like to add a new language, such as Spanish, French, or German, you'll need to send a request to the Onprint Shop technical team.
They'll enable the language on the back end, assign the correct ISO code, add the flag icon, and set the default language if needed.
Please note that admin users can't add or activate new languages directly.
Once the technical team adds them, you'll be able to manage translations using the admin panel.

After you've added new languages, you can view and manage them from the Store configuration menu by opening the Site Settings section and selecting the Languages tab, where all added languages are listed.
When setting up a new language for the first time, you can use the Auto Translate feature to translate existing content across your website automatically.
This process may take a little time depending on the amount of content on your site.
The system will automatically translate sections such as IFAQS, product descriptions, category names, CMS pages, e-mail templates, testimonials, SEO fields, and more.
Later, if you add new content like new products, templates, or CMS pages, just go to that section in your admin panel.
For example, let's navigate to the product description tab, select the language from the floating language menu and either add translations manually or use the auto translate option.
And remember, always click save after making changes so they appear correctly on your storefront.
Now let's talk about managing language specific images.
Just like text, images should also be localized to enhance the browsing experience.
You can upload images for specific languages in multiple areas.
For example, in the product description section, select the desired language before uploading the images.
In the product gallery, choose the language from the drop down menu and then upload the corresponding images.
Similarly, in the banner section, you can upload localized images and banner text by selecting the appropriate language from the drop down menu.
Next, we'll look at translating image all text.
Translating All text help search engines index your images correctly and improves visibility in different languages.
To translate image alt text, go to the SEO Image Alt Text section.
In your admin panel.
You can translate the alt text for product and category images.
Make your selection and then select the language from the floating menu.
Enter the translated text and click Save.
Now let's see how your customers experienced the multilingual storefront.
Once multiple languages are enabled, customers will see a flag icon allowing them to select their preferred language.
The customers can even set their preferred language by navigating to their My Account menu and visiting the profile page on the storefront.

Additionally, the admin can define a default language for each customer by navigating to the Customer module, selecting Website Customers, and then on the Add or Edit page under the Customer Settings section.
Finally, let's talk about auto translation in the Designer Studio.
To enable this, go to Studio Settings and turn on both Enable Text Translation and Enable Auto Translation for Browse Design.
Enabling Text Translation allows customers to translate individual text elements.

For example, when a customer chooses a design to personalize, they can then select the text from the design within the studio, click on the Auto Translation icon from the Quick action pop up, choose the From Enter languages from the left navigation panel, and then click on the Translate button to automatically convert the selected texts.
The Auto Translation for Browse design setting, when enabled, automatically translates the entire design template based on the storefront language selected by the customer.

For example, when a customer chooses a language on the storefront and opens a design template, the designer studio will automatically display the translated version, making the design experience smooth, localized, and easy.
And that's it.
You've now learned how to enable and manage multiple languages.
